The provided data represents the TE360 Master Research Database & Intelligence Registry, a comprehensive collection of sources and tasks related to the "Terminel-Sagasta Investigation" updated as of May 2026.
Key Takeaways

• Extensive Research Infrastructure: The Master Registry contains over 75 unique data sources spanning diverse categories such as the Mexican National Archives (AGN), US National Archives (NARA), mining and geospatial databases, and specialized academic repositories.
• High Digital Accessibility: A significant majority of the sources (51) are categorized as FREE ONLINE, facilitating immediate research. However, 9 sources require MAIL REQUESTS and 4 require IN-PERSON visits, indicating a need for physical archival work.
• Thematic Research "Pipes": The investigation is organized into thematic "Pipes" such as GEO + MIN (Geology and Mining), POL (Politics), and LAND (Land titles and agrarian records), each mapped to specific high-priority databases.
• Active Investigation Queue: The project has an active Priority Action Queue with 20 tasks currently marked as "NOT STARTED". Examples of urgent tasks include:
  • Contacting Carmelita Terango for family oral history.
  • Emailing Thomas Passananti (SDSU) regarding academic collaboration.
  • Hashing private title deeds and letters for digital security.
  • Contacting the Huntington Library and Wells Fargo Historical Services for specific ledger and shipment records.


Data Source Distribution
The following charts visualize the accessibility and prioritization of the research sources within the Master Registry.

The Distribution of Data Sources by Access Type chart highlights that while most data is freely available online, a portion of the research relies on more traditional archival methods like mail and in-person visits.

The Data Sources by Priority Level chart shows that the majority of sources are classified as TIER 2 or TIER 3, with 19 critical TIER 1 sources forming the core of the investigation.
